A complete cycle

The third example, Help › Examples › Rankine cycle, is a whole problem on one sheet: a Rankine cycle with water as the working fluid, an isentropic pump and a turbine with an isentropic efficiency of 0.86. The sheet follows the order of a solution on paper.

Given values

fluid water
p_b   = 70 [bar]       % boiler pressure
T_1   = 520 [C]        % turbine inlet temperature
p_c   = 0.1 [bar]      % condenser pressure
eta_t = 0.86           % turbine isentropic efficiency

These four lines are inputs of the sheet: an input is a line name = number [unit], or a number written in a state line (x = 0 in state 3 makes x_3 an input). The x = 0 of state 3 below is a fifth input. An input can be dragged on a figure when it fixes a state along an axis, and swept in the Sweep view.

States

% No pressure drop in the boiler and condenser: states 4 and 1 are at
% p_b, states 2 and 3 at p_c.
state 1  : p = p_b, T = T_1
% State 2s: the turbine exit if the expansion were isentropic.
state 2s : p = p_c, s = s_1
% The actual exit enthalpy follows from the turbine efficiency.
eta_t = (h_1 - h_2) / (h_1 - h_2s)
state 2  : p = p_c, h = h_2
% State 3: saturated liquid leaves the condenser.
state 3  : p = p_c, x = 0
% State 4: the pump is isentropic, so s_4 = s_3.
state 4  : p = p_b, s = s_3
  1. State 1, the turbine inlet, from the boiler pressure and the turbine inlet temperature.
  2. State 2s, the turbine exit if the expansion were isentropic: the condenser pressure and s_1.
  3. The turbine efficiency is an equation in h_2, the one unknown it holds. Dome solves it, and h_2 then fixes state 2 with the condenser pressure.
  4. State 3, saturated liquid leaving the condenser: x = 0.
  5. State 4, the pump exit: the boiler pressure and s_3, for an isentropic pump.

Work, heat transfer and performance

% Each component: steady state, kinetic and potential energy changes
% neglected. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name.
% Turbine, no stray heat transfer. w_t: turbine work per unit mass
% flowing, Ẇ_t/ṁ.
w_t   = h_1 - h_2      % turbine
% Pump, no stray heat transfer. w_p: pump work per unit mass, Ẇ_p/ṁ.
w_p   = h_4 - h_3      % pump
% Boiler, no work. q_in: heat transfer to the steam per unit mass, Q̇_in/ṁ.
q_in  = h_1 - h_4      % boiler
% Condenser, no work. q_out: heat transfer from the steam per unit
% mass, Q̇_out/ṁ.
q_out = h_2 - h_3      % condenser
% w_net: net work per unit mass, Ẇ_cycle/ṁ.
w_net = w_t - w_p
eta = w_net / q_in     % thermal efficiency
bwr = w_p / w_t        % back work ratio

Each component's energy balance, per unit mass of steam, is one line, after a comment naming the assumptions that reduce the balance to it. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name. The value of each line appears at its right, and the Workspace lists every result with its unit.

The check

check q_in - q_out == w_net

For the cycle as a whole, the net heat transfer equals the net work. The check confirms that the work and heat-transfer lines are consistent with each other; a sign or state-label error makes it fail. It is evaluated after the sheet is solved; the Checks tab shows that it passed. A check that fails is listed as Failed.

The T–s diagram

plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -s- 4 -p- 1

The diagram follows the cycle: expansion 1–2, condensation 2–3 at constant pressure, pumping 3–4, and heating 4–1 at constant pressure. Because s_2 differs from s_1, the path 1–2 is drawn dashed: the actual expansion is not a process at constant entropy, and only its end states are known. The figure appears in the window above.

Changing an input

The last comment of the sheet suggests a change: T_1 = 560 [C]. After the edit, the changed line shows the previous value, the results that changed are tinted, and the T–s diagram draws the previous cycle dashed (see States and diagrams). Sweeps runs the same sheet over a whole range of turbine inlet temperatures.
